**Four areas in the “Experiencing Violence” section that have been trending in the wrong direction (i.e., increasing) across all available years (2013‑2023) are:**

| # | Area | Why it is a “wrong‑direction” trend |
|---|------|-------------------------------------|
| 1 | **Physical violence / being attacked** | The proportion of students reporting being physically taken‑prison or attacked has risen from the early 2010s to 2023. |
| 2 | **Sexual violence / non‑consensual sexual contact** | Reports of sexual victimization (sexual assault or unwanted sexual contact) have shown a steady uptick over the 10‑year period. |
| 3 | **Bullying (including cyber‑bullying)** | The percentage of students who say they have been bullied—whether in person or online—has been climbing. |
| 4 | **Missing school because of safety concerns** | A growing share of students miss school due to worries about safety on the way to or at school, indicating worsening school‑environment safety. |

These four trends reflect growing challenges for youth safety and well‑being in the United States and underscore the need for targeted prevention and support efforts.

**Four areas in the “Experiencing Violence” section that have been trending in the wrong direction (i.e., increasing) across all available years (2013‑2023) are:**

| # | Area | Why it is a “wrong‑direction” trend |
|---|------|-------------------------------------|
| 1 | **Physical violence / being attacked** | The proportion of students reporting being physically taken‑prison or attacked has risen from the early 2010s to 2023. |
| 2 | **Sexual violence / non‑consensual sexual contact** | Reports of sexual victimization (sexual assault or unwanted sexual contact) have shown a steady uptick over the 10‑year period. |
| 3 | **Bullying (including cyber‑bullying)** | The percentage of students who say they have been bullied—whether in person or online—has been climbing. |
| 4 | **Missing school because of safety concerns** | A growing share of students miss school due to worries about safety on the way to or at school, indicating worsening school‑environment safety. |

These four trends reflect growing challenges for youth safety and well‑being in the United States and underscore the need for targeted prevention and support efforts.
